---
title: "Access"
---

There are four ways to reach the data. Use the first one that works for you.

| You are... | Use | Account needed |
|---|---|---|
| Working on the WHOI HPC cluster | Direct path under `{{< var vast_prefix >}}` | WHOI HPC account |
| On a WHOI computer (on site or VPN) | SMB share | WHOI login |
| On the WHOI network or VPN, without HPC or SMB | HTTPS download | None |
| Off site, or moving many files | Globus | Globus login |

## HPC cluster

The store is mounted read-only at `{{< var vast_prefix >}}` on the cluster.
This is the fastest option and the one to use for large analyses: open files
in place with xarray, or through the [intake-esm catalog](catalog.qmd).

```python
import xarray as xr
ds = xr.open_mfdataset(
    "{{< var vast_prefix >}}/cmip6/CMIP/NCAR/CESM2/historical/r1i1p1f1/Amon/tas/gn/1/*.nc"
)
```

## SMB share

From a WHOI laptop or desktop, connect to the share `{{< var smb_path >}}`
(placeholder until IT confirms the share name). The directory layout is the
same as on the cluster.

::: {.callout-tip}
Many people reading the same files over SMB at once has caused errors in the
past. For heavy or parallel reads, work on the cluster instead.
:::

## HTTPS download

Files can be downloaded over HTTPS, with no account, from
`{{< var https_prefix >}}`. This works only from the WHOI network or VPN.
URLs follow the same layout as the store. There is no directory listing: use
the [browser](browse.qmd) to generate a list of file URLs, then follow the
[download guide](download-guide.qmd).

Downloads are rate limited to keep the service available to everyone. For
large transfers, use the cluster or [Globus](#globus).

## Globus {#globus}

[Open the WHOI CMIP collection in Globus]({{< var globus_url >}}) and log in
with Globus. The collection's `/cmip6/data/` folder is
`{{< var vast_prefix >}}`, with the same directory layout, so the paths shown
in the [browser](browse.qmd) work there too. Transfer files to your own
Globus collection; on a laptop, install
[Globus Connect Personal](https://www.globus.org/globus-connect-personal).
Globus is the best choice for moving many files or terabytes off site.

## Public cloud copies

Much of CMIP6 is also available in public cloud storage, which may be faster
than downloading from WHOI if you compute in the cloud:

- [Pangeo / Google Cloud CMIP6](https://pangeo-data.github.io/pangeo-cmip6-cloud/):
  Zarr stores with an intake-esm catalog.
- [AWS Open Data CMIP6](https://registry.opendata.aws/cmip6/): the same
  collection on Amazon S3.
- [ERA5 on AWS](https://registry.opendata.aws/ecmwf-era5/) and other public
  ERA5 mirrors.

Use the WHOI server when you work on the WHOI cluster, need a dataset that is
not in the cloud collections, or need the exact files used in an earlier WHOI
analysis. The cloud copies can differ from ESGF and from each other in version
and format; check `version` and the dataset attributes before mixing sources.
